'''Marcus William Feldman''' (born 14 November 1942) is the Burnet C. and Mildred Finley Wohlford Professor of Biological Sciences, director of the Morrison Institute for Population and Resource Studies, and co-director of the Center for Computational, Evolutionary and Human Genomics (CEHG) at [[Stanford University]].<ref>{{cite web| author= |title=Marcus W. Feldman, MS, PhD |date= | url= http://fsi.stanford.edu/people/marcus_w_feldman |work= fsi.stanford.edu |publisher= Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies, Stanford|accessdate= 2 September 2013}}</ref> He is an Australian-born mathematician turned American theoretical biologist, best known for his mathematical evolutionary theory and [[Computational biomodeling|computational studies]] in [[evolutionary biology]],<ref>{{Scopus|id=35429106600}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Rosenberg | first1 = N. A. | authorlink = Noah Rosenberg| last2 = Pritchard | first2 = J. K. | authorlink2 = Jonathan K. Pritchard| last3 = Weber | first3 = J. L. | last4 = Cann | first4 = H. M. | last5 = Kidd | first5 = K. K. | last6 = Zhivotovsky | first6 = L. A. | last7 = Feldman | first7 = M. W. | authorlink7 = Marcus Feldman| title = Genetic Structure of Human Populations | journal = Science | volume = 298 | issue = 5602| pages = 2381–2385| year = 2002 | url = https://web.stanford.edu/group/rosenberglab/papers/popstruct.pdf| doi = 10.1126/science.1078311 | pmid=12493913|bibcode = 2002Sci...298.2381R | s2cid = 8127224 }}</ref> and for originating with [[Luigi Luca Cavalli-Sforza|L. L. Cavalli-Sforza]] the theory of cultural evolution.

==Early life and education==

Marcus Feldman was born and raised in [[Perth]], Australia. His father Simon Feldman was an engineer, and this inspired him to take up mathematics. He studied at the [[University of Western Australia]] from where he [[matriculated]] in 1959, and graduated (with majors in mathematics and statistics) in 1964. In 1966 he obtained Master of Science degree in mathematics from [[Monash University]]. He went abroad to US to join a PhD programme at Stanford University. He earned his degree in 1969 under the supervision of [[Samuel Karlin]] in the Department of Mathematics.<ref>{{cite web| author= |title= Marc Feldman|date= | url= https://fsi9-prod.s3.us-west-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/staff/3234/Marcus_Feldman-CV.pdf|accessdate= 8 December 2025}}</ref>

==Professional career==
{{more references|section|date=February 2026}}
After a brief work at Stanford as a research assistant for Karlin, and as acting assistant professor in the Department of Biology, Feldman returned to Australia to join at [[La Trobe University]] as a lecturer of mathematics. In 1971 he was appointed as assistant professor in the Department of Biological Sciences at Stanford. With [[L.L. Cavalli-Sforza]] in 1973, he originated the quantitative theory of cultural evolution, initiating a research program in cultural transmission and gene-culture [[coevolution]].{{cn|date=February 2026}} His own research into human molecular evolution such as in [[China]] led him to international recognition.{{cn|date=February 2026}} He is the author of more than 625 scientific papers and several books on evolution, ecology, and mathematical biology.{{cn|date=February 2026}}

In addition, he is the founding editor of ''[[Theoretical Population Biology]]'' (1971–2013) and an associate editor of ''[[Genetics (journal)|Genetics]]'', ''[[Human Genetics (journal)|Human Genetics]]'', ''[[Annals of Human Genetics]]'', ''[[Annals of Human Biology]]'', and ''[[Complexity (journal)|Complexity]]''. He was the editor of ''[[The American Naturalist]]'' from 1984 to 1990. He was a member of the board of trustees at the [[Santa Fe Institute]] from 1984 to 2006.<ref>{{cite web|author= |title= Vita: MARCUS WILLIAM FELDMAN|date= 2013|url= http://www-evo.stanford.edu/Feldman-cv.pdf|work= www-evo.stanford.edu|publisher= Department of Biology, Stanford University|accessdate= 3 September 2013|archive-date= 10 June 2020|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200610105658/http://www-evo.stanford.edu/Feldman-cv.pdf|url-status= dead}}</ref>
